title: Coefficient properties of the image of a complete local PID
statement: Let R be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal m. Let C be a local principal ideal domain, complete for its maximal ideal n [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with n=pC for a natural number p. Suppose f: C -> R is a ring map with f^{-1}(m)=n and residue_R composed with f surjective. Then L=f(C) is local, its maximal ideal equals L intersect m, L is complete for that ideal, the induced map L/(L intersect m) -> R/m is bijective, and L intersect m=pL.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A(1), image verification of Definition Tag 0326; completeness via Lemmas 031B and 00MA(3)

proof.text: The surjection C -> f.range makes f.range local. The image of the maximal ideal of C is its maximal ideal. By the assumed comap identity and the map-comap identity for a surjection, this image is exactly the comap of m along the subring inclusion. Mapping the generator p shows that this ideal is generated by p in the image.

C is Noetherian because it is a PID. Give f.range its C-algebra structure through the range-restriction map. Surjectivity makes it a finite C-module. Apply finite_module_complete_over_complete_noetherian to this module and the maximal ideal of C. IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff identifies this with completeness for the mapped ideal, already identified with the intersection ideal.

The quotient map for a comap ideal is injective. For each residue y, lift y through the assumed surjective composite C -> R -> R/m. The class of f.rangeRestrict of that lift is a preimage under the quotient map, proving surjectivity.
